topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture opens with framing remarks introducing cancer therapy and outlining the primary learning outcomes.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore standard local and systemic treatment modalities, including surgery, radiotherapy, cytotoxic chemotherapies, and the physiological and cellular mechanisms underlying treatment resistance.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic signaling, checkpoint, and DNA repair vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies designed to exploit cancer-specific biological vulnerabilities, including hormone receptor dependency, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction, kinase inhibitors, and resistance pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address targeted therapies directed against hyperactive oncogenic kinases, their molecular mechanisms of inhibition, and the adaptive resistance and addiction mechanisms that arise.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on utilizing engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to selectively direct cytotoxic effects against tumor surface markers.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell redirection strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine natural immune surveillance against cancer and various immunotherapeutic interventions designed to harness and redirect T cells against tumor antigens.

topics.label: Therapeutic challenges, clinical progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the overarching challenges facing cancer medicine, the clinical progress achieved across historical treatment eras, and emerging dilemmas for future oncology.
